content:
alex: Heads-up — ran the replay harness against 2.1.0 runtime and saw a 22% tail latency regression vs synthetic rps runs. Sharing notes.
sam: hmm, where does the regression show up? p50/p95/p99?
maria: p50 ~ same, p95 +18%, p99 +22% on sequences >512 tokens. CPU on host didn't spike.
alex: interesting: with synthetic (keepalive pooled connections) we get expected numbers. Replay harness opens ~1 conn per session and replays historical inter-request timing. That difference looks correlated.
tony: could be TLS handshake and Nagle interaction on short-lived conns — lots of small writes + TLS record coalescing causes stall.
alex: yes, capture from tcpdump shows many small TLS records for prompt init. When pooling enabled the adapter coalesces into fewer packets.
sam: also: replayed sessions hit cold KV cache more often because sequence prefixes vary. That increases dynamic kernel selection overhead and more cache misses.
maria: do we have traces showing kernel selection frequency? infra-bot: kernel-selection:event count=1.8x for replay vs synth; avg decision latency +4ms.
alex: pasted minimal repro of client spawn in harness:
```
# replay harness snippet
for s in sessions:
  conn = http1.connect(host)  # not pooled
  resp = conn.post('/v1/generate', json=payload)
  time.sleep(s.inter_request_gap)
```
sam: try switching to HTTP/1.1 keepalive and a pool of 100 conns, and run same session timing but reusing conns. If perf matches synth -> client-side artifact.
tony: note: gRPC path behaves differently because multiplexed streams => fewer TLS handshakes and smaller per-request overhead. But gRPC also changes batching heuristics server-side: we see larger automatic batching (more requests per batch) because connections have steady streams.
maria: so apples-to-apples means: match connection churn, TLS session reuse, and request coalescing. Also align prompt length distribution so KV cache hit rate is comparable.
alex: for fairness we added a shim in harness that preserves original session timing but reuses the same pooled conn for sessions from same user. That brought p99 down to +3% vs synth.
sam: good. Any CPU hotspots from profiling? alex: profiler shows more time in kernel-selection evaluation and small memcpy on kv cache load for replay cold bursts. Kernel-selection invoked more because sequence length variance prevented reuse of previous kernel choice.
maria: can we add a deterministic kernel pin for the test to isolate kernel selection cost? tony: yes, we exposed env RL_RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fast16 and pinned quant path. With that, replay vs synth delta disappears almost entirely.
alex: action items: 1) update replay harness doc to recommend pooled connections by default + TLS session reuse; 2) add a toggle to fix kernel selection to measure pure runtime perf; 3) record KV cache hit distribution in harness outputs (histogram).
sam: also add a short note about Nagle/TLS: small writes then flush causes extra latency on short-lived conns. Recommend disabling Nagle at client or use TCP_CORK semantics or increase write coalescing window in harness.
maria: +1 on adding KV cache histograms. We should also add a canary test that emulates realistic client behavior: intermittent short sessions with high prefix variance to catch regressions.
tony: I'll open a PR with harness changes and a checklist for apples-to-apples comparisons. I'll tag you @alex @maria for review.
alex: thanks — will attach packet captures and profile flamegraphs to the PR. :thumbsup:
